source.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent Optimizes Over-parameterized Deep ReLU Networks
source.authors: Difan Zou; Yuan Cao; Dongruo Zhou; Quanquan Gu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves convergence results for deep fully connected ReLU networks, using a different setting and theoretical analysis from the benchmark claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical results under stated assumptions, not experiments on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 or corrupted or random labels. It does not compare widths or initialization schemes empirically.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional convergence for fully connected ReLU networks on binary classification data. V1 specifies convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; the study provides no results for those systems or datasets. Its results also do not test the comparisons or dynamics named in V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion. More precisely, they prove arbitrarily small training loss and, when the loss at zero margin is positive, zero training classification error for sufficiently wide fully connected deep ReLU networks under their assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theoretical convergence guarantees for fully connected networks on binary classification data under separation assumptions; it does not run benchmark experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The result depends on sufficient width, Gaussian initialization, data separation, loss-function assumptions and learning-rate conditions; SGD also requires the additional Assumption 4.4.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollaries 4.3 and 4.6 guarantee zero training classification error with high probability for sufficiently wide fully connected ReLU networks under specified data, initialization, loss and optimization assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently over-parameterized fully connected deep ReLU networks can achieve zero binary training classification error using randomly initialized GD or SGD under data separation and suitable optimization conditions.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and conditional on data, architecture, loss, width and learning-rate assumptions. It does not establish empirical benchmark performance or results for corrupted/random labels.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and the effects of smaller models, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization or Fixup.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical guarantees are substantive, but extending V1 to include fully connected networks would require restating that version. Assumed Gaussian initialization and sufficient width do not themselves test initialization comparisons or narrow teacher-student width effects.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. It analyzes binary classification on separated training data with sufficiently wide fully connected ReLU networks.

rows.note: The corollary states zero training error when loss at zero is positive; the result is theoretical and conditional on the paper's assumptions.
rows.check: Corollary 4.3 does establish zero training classification error under its assumptions, but for fully connected networks, outside V1's specified systems and datasets. Layer widths need only be comparable, with maximum width at most twice minimum width; they need not all equal m. Loss coverage requires all assumptions, including global smoothness; the text's examples of hinge and exponential loss concern Assumption 3.2 alone.

rows.check: Corollary 4.6 establishes conditional zero training classification error for fully connected networks, outside V1. Widths need only be comparable. The recorded learning rate comes from Lemma 5.6; Theorem 4.5 states O(n^-3 L^-9 m^-1), while its proof ultimately chooses O(phi m^-1 n^(2p-7) L^-9 B^2). Preserve this discrepancy rather than presenting the lemma's rate as the complete corollary recipe.
